category: # Parts list for revision G. We haven't sourced any of it yet - every price vendor and link is TBD.
# Motors igniters and eggs are deliberately not here. They come out of a separate budget so keeping
# them off this list stops us double-counting. Don't add them.
# Careful with the egg capsule: the 170 g budget in the sim includes the two eggs themselves so the
# foam and bulkheads together have to come in under that.
# Rows marked UNDESIGNED are in the sim as a lumped mass but have no geometry no material and no CAD.
# They're the biggest sourcing risk on this list.
# This isn't a complete list yet - it covers what's named in the rev G configuration and no more.

spec: Ogive 230 mm; 66 mm dia aft; 1.5 mm wall polystyrene; 35 mm aft shoulder
notes: Fully specified in the model. Holds the 42 g of nose ballast.
The primary section. 320 mm clears the 300 mm minimum in the rules.
Material and how we make it are both TBD.
Carries the fins. Far enough from 66 mm to satisfy the 9 mm rule.
Sized for the 24 x 95 mm motor. Retention method TBD.
Planform is 95 root / 40 tip / 55 semispan / 50 sweep in mm. Cant is 0.0 deg in the sim; 0.5 deg is under consideration but not committed. Sheet size to buy is TBD.

UNDESIGNED - nothing drawn no material chosen no CAD. Part of the 170 g / 130 mm x 61 mm capsule budget at top+20 mm. Second heaviest thing in the rocket and the CG stability margins and nose ballast all assume that 170 g is right.
UNDESIGNED - no material picked and no retention method. Has to fully enclose two 55-63 g eggs to satisfy the payload rule. Same mass risk as the bulkheads.
42 g is fixed. Material and how it's retained are TBD. This is the number that moves if the capsule mass turns out not to be 170 g.
Sized to land inside the 37-40 s band. Line length and attachment TBD.
Holds the chute closed to trim the descent. Release altitude TBD.
IMPLIED - the fin can decision refers to plywood already being in the design but we never wrote down the thickness the grade or which parts are made from it.
IMPLIED - the jig exists to hold fins while this cures but which epoxy and the cure schedule are both TBD.
IMPLIED - we quote 14.0 m/s off a 6 ft rail but there's no rail button or launch lug anywhere in rev G.
For the fin jig. About 50 g per print at 4 walls and 20 percent infill roughly 4 hours. Solid volume would be about 151 g. Tooling only so it adds no flight mass.
